name: Aeneid
info: The Aeneid is a Latin epic poem by Virgil, written between 29 and 19 BC, telling how the Trojan Aeneas fled Troy and reached Italy to become ancestor of the Romans; it became central to Latin education.

facts.made: Virgil, Roman poet, under Augustus and with Maecenas as his patron; published after his death by his literary executors Lucius Varius Rufus and Plotius Tucca on Augustus' order
facts.form: A Latin epic of 9,896 lines in dactylic hexameter, in twelve books of roughly 700 to 900 lines each, left unfinished
facts.where: Read in printed editions and in translations into many languages
facts.known: Arma virumque cano; Dido and Aeneas; the descent to the underworld; pietas and furor; the founding myth of Rome; Virgil as Dante's guide

t: Virgil shaped scattered older tales of Aeneas into a founding myth that tied Rome to Troy and the family of Julius Caesar to its heroes and gods.
The first six books follow the wanderings from Troy to Italy, after the Odyssey, and the last six the war in Latium, after the Iliad.
Unfinished at Virgil's death in 19 BC, it was published on Augustus' order and became a cornerstone of Latin education for centuries.
dyk: Virgil died with the poem unfinished and wished the manuscript burned; Augustus ordered his executors to disregard the wish and publish it with as few changes as possible. Its many half-complete lines and abrupt ending are read as signs that it was never finished.
ev: Greek vases already show accounts of Aeneas founding a new home in Etruria
Virgil dies at Brundisium with the poem unfinished; Augustus orders it published
The grammarian Maurus Servius Honoratus writes the most complete ancient commentary on the poem
Gavin Douglas completes his Eneados, the first full and faithful rendering in an Anglic language
Henry Purcell's opera Dido and Aeneas is performed
Ivan Kotliarevsky writes Eneida, a mock-heroic burlesque in the Ukrainian language

sections.origins:
The story of Aeneas reaching Italy predates Virgil by centuries. As Greek settlements spread from the sixth century BC, colonists tied their new homes to their existing myths, and the fall of Troy suited the purpose. The legend combined Greek, Etruscan, Latin and Roman elements: Greek vases of the sixth century BC already show Aeneas founding a new home in Etruria, he was worshipped at Lavinium, and a fragment usually attributed to Hellanicus of Lesbos made him the founder of Rome with the help of Odysseus. The Romans most likely took a full interest in these Greek myths after the war against Pyrrhus of Epirus in 280 BC.

Virgil wrote in a time of great change, after the fall of the Roman Republic and the civil wars ending at Actium, when the new emperor Augustus was promoting peace and a return to traditional Roman values. He took the scattered tales of Aeneas, a figure known since the Iliad but with no fixed character beyond his pietas, and made of them a national epic that tied Rome to Troy, explained the Punic Wars and presented the Julio-Claudian line as descendants of the founders and gods of Rome and Troy.
sections.content:
The poem opens with Arma virumque cano, of arms and the man I sing, and begins in the middle of things with the Trojan fleet driven by a storm that the goddess Juno has raised. Shipwrecked in Africa, Aeneas tells Dido, queen of the new city of Carthage, of the wooden horse, the sack of Troy, the loss of his wife Creusa and his wanderings round the Mediterranean. Dido falls in love with him, but Jupiter sends Mercury to remind him of his duty; when he sails, she kills herself on a pyre and calls for eternal strife between their peoples. After funeral games in Sicily, Aeneas descends with the Cumaean Sibyl into the underworld, where his father Anchises shows him the future of Rome.

In the second half Aeneas settles in Latium, where King Latinus is told by oracles to give his daughter Lavinia to a stranger rather than to Turnus of the Rutuli. Juno stirs up war. Aeneas gains allies from Evander, at the site of the future Rome, and a shield made by Vulcan showing Rome's history; Turnus kills Evander's son Pallas. The poem ends when Aeneas, about to spare the defeated Turnus, sees Pallas' belt on him and kills him in rage.
sections.making:
Virgil wrote the Aeneid between 29 and 19 BC, and legend held that he wrote only three lines a day. It is composed in dactylic hexameter, each line of six feet made of dactyls and spondees, with a metre based on the length of syllables. Its twelve books fall into two halves, books 1 to 6 commonly linked with Homer's Odyssey and books 7 to 12 with the Iliad, reflecting Virgil's ambition to rival Homer, though the correspondence is rough; the narrative can also be read in three groups of four books, on Dido, the arrival in Italy and the war. Virgil's Latin has been praised for its evenness, subtlety and dignity, and he uses alliteration, assonance, metaphor and simile to build tension.

According to tradition Virgil travelled to Greece around 19 BC to revise the poem, met Augustus at Athens, caught a fever near Megara and died at Brundisium on his way home, wishing the manuscript burned. Some legends say he had come to dislike a passage in book 8. Augustus ordered his executors Lucius Varius Rufus and Plotius Tucca to publish it with few changes. The half-complete lines and abrupt ending are generally taken as evidence that it was unfinished.
sections.reception:
The poem appears to have been a success from the start. Virgil is said to have recited books 2, 4 and 6 to Augustus, and the mention of Marcellus in book 6 apparently caused Augustus' sister Octavia to faint. By the 2nd century AD at the latest it had become an essential part of a Latin education, usually memorised, and it stayed central after the decline of the Roman Empire. In Latin-Christian culture it was a canonical text studied with commentaries, the most complete written by the 4th-century grammarian Maurus Servius Honoratus.

Critics have long debated its tone. Some read it as pessimistic and subversive of the Augustan regime, others as a celebration of the new dynasty; many see Aeneas, founder of Rome, as a figure for Augustus, its re-founder, and its prophecies and the shield's picture of Actium as support for him. Its themes of pietas, fate and divine intervention, and Aeneas' final killing of Turnus in furor, have been read as an unfinished Roman ideal or as a comment on the violence of the late Republican civil wars. The exit from the underworld through the ivory gate of false dreams is among its most disputed passages.
sections.survival:
Because the Aeneid was composed and preserved in writing rather than orally, its text shows less variation than other classical epics. Its survival was tied to the schoolroom: from antiquity through the Middle Ages it was copied, taught and commented on as a basic text of Latin learning, and from 1600 to 1900 the Latin school stood at the centre of European education, with Virgil taught at the advanced level. In the United States it was taught in the fourth year of Latin at least until the 1960s.

Its unfinished ending led later writers to complete it. The 15th-century poet Maffeo Vegio wrote a Thirteenth Book, widely printed in the Renaissance; Pier Candido Decembrio began another; and modern supplements include Claudio Salvucci's The Laviniad of 1994 and Ursula K. Le Guin's novel Lavinia of 2008. Translations carried it into the vernaculars: Gavin Douglas's Scots Eneados of 1513, John Dryden's English version, partial versions by Henry Howard, Earl of Surrey, and Seamus Heaney, and many modern verse translations, among them those of Cecil Day-Lewis, Robert Fitzgerald, Robert Fagles and Sarah Ruden.
sections.legacy:
The Aeneid is a cornerstone of the Western canon and was long held to be the summit of Latin literature, as the Iliad was of Greek. Its influence has been traced in Beowulf, Layamon's Brut, The Faerie Queene and Milton's Paradise Lost, and in Os Lusíadas by Luís de Camões. Dante quoted and alluded to it throughout the Divine Comedy and made Virgil his guide through the Inferno and Purgatorio. Phrases from it entered Latin as Shakespeare's did English, such as Sunt lacrimae rerum, the tears of things.

It has been retold on the stage and screen: Henry Purcell's opera Dido and Aeneas of 1688 with its lament When I am laid in earth, Hector Berlioz's Les Troyens, Italian film and television versions, and Brian Friel's play Translations, which ends with a passage from it. It also invited parody, from Paul Scarron's French travesty, which spread across Europe, to Ivan Kotliarevsky's Eneida of 1798, considered the first literary work published wholly in modern Ukrainian and made into an animated film in 1991. In the United States its Latin lines remain part of the Advanced Placement Latin syllabus.

summary: The Aeneid is Virgil's Latin epic of the Trojan Aeneas, who flees burning Troy, loses Dido and wins a home in Italy as ancestor of the Romans. Written under Augustus and left unfinished in 19 BC, it was published on the emperor's order and has shaped Latin education and European literature ever since.
